title: Verify emailVerified (or the invite_token) before granting tutor-invite acceptance by email match

evidence.quote: // This prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them.
// without needing the emailed deep link. Match the caller's verified email.

why: Firebase Auth lets anyone register an account with any unverified email string. acceptTutorInvite, declineTutorInvite, and listTutorGrants({mode:'pending_for_me'}) all authorize 'is this caller the invited tutor' purely by comparing the caller's Auth email to grant.tutor_email -- none of them checks callerRecord.emailVerified (or the token claim), despite comments at both call sites explicitly (and incorrectly) claiming this 'prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them' / matches the 'verified' email. An attacker who front-runs registration of the invited tutor's email address can call listTutorGrants(pending_for_me) to discover the grantId, then acceptTutorInvite to gain ongoing read access (and any write permissions the parent granted) to the child's full learning profile -- without ever proving ownership of that inbox. The invite_token generated specifically to prevent exactly this (comment: 'single-use, per NFR-3') is stored on the grant doc but is never read back or compared anywhere in the file, so it provides zero actual protection. cf_grant_invite.test.mjs's own header comment confirms this exact gate is never exercised by any test.
recommendation: Require callerRecord.emailVerified === true in acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite before trusting the email match, and/or require the caller to supply invite_token and compare it against grant.invite_token (the mechanism already built for this). Apply the same emailVerified gate to listTutorGrants' pending_for_me query so an unverified account cannot even discover invites addressed to an email it doesn't own.
acceptance_criteria: A new Auth-emulator-backed test in cf_grant_invite.test.mjs seeds an unverified-email account and asserts acceptTutorInvite rejects it (e.g. permission-denied).
acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite check emailVerified or invite_token before authorizing by email match.
make test-functions (or a new CI job per the companion finding) seeds Auth-emulator users so this path is actually exercised, not skipped.

corrections: The finding's rule citation "SR-5 (tutor cross-user access)" is imprecise: SR-5's literal text (coding-standards.md:313) governs Firestore *security rules* (state/expiry checks in firestore.rules), not Cloud Functions callable-auth logic. The doc has no explicit rule for CF invite-acceptance identity verification, so this is a thematic/nearest-analog citation rather than a verbatim match. Does not weaken the underlying defect, which is real and severe.

The cited rule ID "SR-5" is imprecise -- SR-5 in coding-standards.md is specifically about Firestore *security rules* checking grant state/expiry via get(), not about Cloud Function email-verification gates. There is no exactly-matching named rule; the defect falls under the general "Privacy & Child Data" child-privacy principle the finding also cites in its rule field. This labeling looseness doesn't undermine the substance -- the underlying defect is independently verified as real via direct code tracing.
